title: All‑hands: short notice soft quota shift — talking notes (scratch)
content:
Purpose (one line):
A very short, empathetic all‑hands mini‑update to explain why we’re temporarily applying a conservative, soft quota shift on burst rates for non‑paid accounts this week, what to expect, and how we’ll roll back.

Why this matters (speak to engineers + product folks):
- Background: Over the last 36 hours we’ve observed sustained unusual traffic patterns from a small number of free-tier workloads that are crowding the scheduling plane and increasing cold‑start tail latency for paying customers on Dedicated pools.
- Risk: If we don’t act, tail latency could breach our internal SLOs and potentially trigger downstream rate‑limit escalations and increased unit cost from emergency bursts.
- Goal: Buy a soft safety margin (48–72 hours) while infra teams apply targeted mitigations (hot‑key eviction policy, short‑term autoscale policy tweak, and a deploy that adjusts prewarming heuristics).

Core message (3 sentences):
We’re making a temporary, conservative change to burst quotas for non‑paid/free accounts to stabilize latency for production customers. This is a short window measure while infra teams finish a fix that prevents noisy tenants from monopolizing prewarmed capacity. We expect normal burst behavior to resume once the deploys have validated (target: 48–72 hours).

What to say in the all‑hands (5 bullets):
- Quick context: unusual traffic from a small set of free workloads caused disproportionate queueing in serving pools.
- Action: we’re applying a non‑disruptive soft cap to free‑tier burst allowance and increasing monitoring thresholds.
- Impact: paid / Dedicated customers are prioritized — you should see improved tail latency and fewer request retries. Free users may see slightly slower warm‑up for large bursts.
- Timeline: immediate; we’ll review metrics at +24h, +48h, and plan rollback at +72h if stable.
- Follow up: postmortem + remediation plan in Confluence, and a short FAQ for support.

Manager/IC script (for small team syncs and Slack):
- TL;DR: temporary soft quota for free accounts to protect production latency. No action needed from most teams. If you own a public demo or scheduled demo this week, please surface it via the #ops‑incidents channel so we can whitelist if needed.

Suggested Slack announcement (short):
Heads up: we’re applying a short‑lived, conservative burst cap for free accounts to stabilize tail latency for paying customers while infra finishes a fix. Expect improvements for Dedicated customers; free demos may see slower large bursts. Monitoring and rollback plan in Confluence: <link>.

Anticipated Q&A (prep answers):
Q: Will paying customers be affected?
A: No — paid/Dedicated SKUs are prioritized and should see equal or better latency. The caps apply only to non‑paid/free burst windows.

Q: How long will this last?
A: Aim is 48–72 hours. We’ll evaluate at 24/48 hours and announce rollback criteria (stable tail latency and no repeat noisy tenants).

Q: Will this change billing?
A: No billing changes — this is a throttling/soft cap on instantaneous burst allotment only. Usage meters still record tokens normally.

Q: Could this break demos or public apps?
A: Possibly for big demo loads that rely on large cold bursts. If you have an imminent demo, file a quick ticket (JIRA-1204) with a time window and we’ll consider a temporary exception.

Operational notes for SRE/infra (bullet list):
- Deploys to watch: prewarm‑heuristic v3.1.2 (rolling), hotkey‑eviction policy tweak (feature flag), autoscale latency threshold bump.
- KPIs to monitor: p95/p99 token latency, queue length, prewarm hit rate, Dedicated pool error rate.
- Rollback criteria: p99 token latency within 10% of baseline for three consecutive 10‑minute windows, no new noisy tenant > 20% of pool for 2 hours.

Follow‑ups and owners (quick):
- Caleb: draft external support FAQ and update Confluence page (deadline: +12h).
- Maya: coordinate infra deploys and post deploy signal checks (+6h).
- Sasha: triage inbound Slack & surface exceptions for demos (+ongoing).
- Devon: prepare short postmortem draft and timeline (+72h or earlier if rollback).

Notes to self (fragments):
- Keep tone calm, avoid technical blame, center on protecting customer SLAs.
- Avoid promising exact rollback windows — frame as contingent on metric validation.
- Post an example support message that CS can paste into customer threads.

Support canned message (for CS):
Hi — we’re temporarily applying a conservative burst cap to free accounts to protect latency for production customers. This should not affect billed usage; if you see errors or have an upcoming demo, please reply with your org and demo time and we will investigate immediate exceptions. Thank you for your patience.

Open questions (for follow up):
- Do we want a proactive email to paid customers or only an internal note? (pros/cons)
- Any legal/regulatory implications for throttling free accounts in region EU‑1? Ask security/compliance.

End scratch — use, edit, or prune.
excerpt: Short draft notes for a calm all‑hands announcement about a short soft quota shift to protect production latency. Includes talking points, Q&A, slack copy, owners.
